name: cell-cell-coupling-spatial
title: Cell–Cell Coupling, Spatial
question:
Does the paper's §Cell–cell coupling viability-negotiation pattern (no dedicated
figure) hold as real spatial multicellularity — multiple CPM cells sharing one diffusing
nutrient field, each running its own dynamic-FBA step at its own footprint, producing both
competitive exclusion and cross-feeding — when the whole colony is composed from independent
frameworks through one N-cell coupling process (`CpmColonyField`), rather than the lumped
two-role, shared-scalar-pool stand-in `draft-to-living-cell`'s §Cell–cell coupling study used?
biological_summary:
This is the spatial realization of the paper's §Cell–cell coupling pattern
(no dedicated figure), built on the flagship's `CpmCellField` process
generalized to `CpmColonyField` — one process instance that owns N CPM cells sharing one
spatio-flux field grid, running one dynamic-FBA step per cell at its own lattice footprint each
tick, and writing all N cells' uptake/secretion deltas back into the shared field as one summed
update. The additive two-writer assumption this depends on (two cells' disjoint footprint
deltas summing correctly into one shared `map[array]` fields store, conserving mass) is no
longer an assumption — it is runtime-verified directly (`tests/test_cpm_colony_two_writer.py`):
two synthetic single-pixel writers on disjoint pixels are each applied independently and sum
losslessly over repeated ticks.

Two tuned regimes over the same `CpmColonyField` process demonstrate both branches of the
paper's §Cell–cell coupling negotiation (no dedicated figure). COMPETITION (`meta_modelers_guide.composites.cellcell-compete`): two glucose
competitors seeded on a uniform 3.0 mM glucose field, differing only in uptake capacity
(`glucose_vmax` 10.0 vs 4.0). Measured over a 20-tick run
(`tests/test_cellcell_regimes.py::test_competition_excludes_the_slower_cell`,
`tests/test_cpm_colony_field.py`): the faster competitor ends with biomass 237.9 against the
slower competitor's 64.5 — a 3.69x margin — and CPM lattice volume 3511 px against 81 px, an
even starker asymmetry, because CPM growth compounds superlinearly once one cell has
out-competed the other for the shared glucose. The shared field is measurably drawn down by
both cells drawing on the same pool, and the loser is displaced to a small fragment (81 px) of
the lattice it started with parity on. This is asymmetric growth under shared-resource
competition — a trend TOWARD competitive exclusion, not exclusion reached: the loser's biomass
still GREW from its 1.25 seed to 64.5 (~51.6x) and stays far above any viable-biomass floor, so
it is spatially DISPLACED, not driven below a viability bound (this study imposes no death and
no viability constraint on a losing cell). And the winner's 3511 px is ~97.5% of the 3600-px
lattice, with the field nearly exhausted by t=20 — the endpoint is as much a finite-size
lattice-saturation artifact as a biological one (by t≈30 the winner fills the whole lattice and
the still-viable loser is simply crowded off it, evicted rather than starved). This is exactly
the paper's §Cell–cell coupling distinction that "what is coupled is not only state, but
constraint": these cells couple STATE (one shared field) but no viability CONSTRAINT, so strict
exclusion is out of reach here — spatial competition as a direct, unscripted consequence of two
independent dFBA solves reading the same depleting field.

CROSS-FEEDING (`meta_modelers_guide.composites.cellcell-crossfeed`) is the biology that carries
this investigation's deepest claim: the paper's §Cell–cell coupling closes on the idea that an
environmental variable acquires its significance relationally — the same molecule counts as
nutrient, signal, or toxin only through its consequences for a given cell's viability. Acetate
embodies exactly that here. It is the glucose-fermenting secretor's metabolic WASTE — a
byproduct it dumps into the shared field — and, at the very same instant, the consumer's sole
carbon FOOD, the only thing keeping it alive. One molecule, two opposite meanings, each set
relationally by the cell whose interface it meets. This is textbook microbial metabolic
cooperation / cross-feeding (morris2013): a byproduct of one organism's metabolism becomes an
obligate resource for another, and a spatial community is knit together by the exchange. The
regime realizes it concretely: a glucose-to-acetate
secretor (O2 cap 5, seeded at a localized 20 mM glucose depot in lattice columns 0-18) paired
with an acetate-consuming cell (`acetate_vmax` 20) seeded well outside the glucose depot
(columns 22-30), with acetate diffusing far faster than glucose in this regime (diffusion
coefficient 15.0 vs 0.4) so the secreted byproduct plume can reach the consumer before the
glucose gradient does. Measured over the same 20-tick run
(`tests/test_cellcell_regimes.py::test_crossfeeding_keeps_the_consumer_viable`): the consumer's
own local glucose reads 0.0 — it genuinely cannot touch glucose — while its local acetate reads
1.30, and its biomass climbs from an initial 1.25 to 3.79 (roughly 3x) on that acetate alone,
ending as a viable cell occupying 65 lattice pixels. The consumer's growth is back-loaded to
the last several ticks of the run, once the secretor's plume has had time to diffuse the
distance between the two cells' footprints — growth is monotonic over the window measured, not
smoothly exponential from tick 0. That the secretor's acetate is what CAUSES this growth — not
anything intrinsic to the consumer or the field — is closed by a secretor-knockout necessity
control (`meta_modelers_guide.composites.cellcell-crossfeed-knockout`): the same composite with
the secretor cell removed so NO acetate is ever produced. Run 20 ticks, the otherwise-identical
consumer (now the only cell) sits at local acetate 0.0 and its biomass never climbs off its
1.25 seed — it persists on the lattice (~35 px) but flatly fails to grow, the genuine negative
control for the handoff. This same acetate carries the arc across the investigation:
waste-and-food here, it becomes a TOXIN in `disintegration-spatial`, where a high local acetate
concentration crosses a cell's viability bound and triggers its collapse — one molecule, three
relational meanings across the two studies.
claim:
Composing N real CPM cells with one shared, real spatio-flux nutrient field through a
single N-cell coupling process (`CpmColonyField`) reproduces the paper's §Cell–cell coupling
viability-negotiation pattern (no dedicated figure) as genuine spatial multicellularity, not a
scripted or lumped stand-in for it: over
20-tick runs, an uptake-capacity asymmetry alone (glucose_vmax 10 vs 4) drives asymmetric
growth toward competitive exclusion (biomass 237.9 vs 64.5, a 3.69x margin; volume 3511 vs 81
px — the loser displaced but still viable, above its 1.25 seed, not driven below a viability
bound), while a
different composite over the same coupling process — a localized glucose depot, a fast-diffusing
acetate byproduct, and an acetate-consuming role — sustains a cell that never touches glucose
(local glucose 0.0) purely via a diffusing cross-feeding handoff (local acetate 1.30, biomass
1.25 -> 3.79). Both regimes run through the same process; only the composite's cell roles and
field constants differ, mirroring `draft-to-living-cell/cell-cell-coupling`'s law-4 pattern
(two handler environments negotiate the shared-resource constraint differently over one
interface) at real spatial, per-footprint metabolic resolution.
key_assumptions:
e_coli_core-derived constants (`glucose_vmax` 10.0/4.0 for the two competitors,
`acetate_vmax` 20 for the consumer, `grow_per_biomass` 30, the O2 cap of 5 on the secretor) are
toy-real: plausible, hand-tuned magnitudes chosen to make competitive exclusion and cross-
feeding both legible over a short (20-tick) run, not fitted to a named organism or medium.

The cross-feeding regime's acetate/glucose diffusion ratio (15.0 vs 0.4) is directionally
defensible — acetate is a smaller molecule and diffuses faster than glucose in real aqueous
media — but the specific ratio was chosen to make the byproduct plume legibly reach the
consumer within a 20-tick run, not fitted to measured diffusion coefficients. Likewise the
cross-feeding regime's localized 20 mM glucose depot (columns 0-18 only, with the consumer
seeded outside it at columns 22-30) is a deliberately engineered spatial arrangement chosen so
the consumer genuinely sees zero glucose (local_glucose == 0.0), not a naturally arising
gradient.

The consumer's growth under cross-feeding is back-loaded to roughly the last 5 ticks of the
20-tick run, once the secretor's acetate plume has had time to diffuse across the distance
separating the two cells' footprints — growth is monotonic over the measured window but is not
a smooth exponential from tick 0, and a shorter run would show less of it.

Each CPM cell in `CpmColonyField` gets its own independent cobra model copy, not one shared
model instance across the colony — avoiding any risk of one cell's dFBA solve silently
perturbing another's solver state, at the cost of N times the per-tick FBA solve cost.

The additive two-writer assumption `CpmColonyField` depends on — that disjoint per-cell
footprint deltas can be summed into one shared `map[array]` fields store and conserve mass — is
no longer taken on faith; it is runtime-verified directly by
`tests/test_cpm_colony_two_writer.py` against two synthetic single-pixel writers on disjoint
pixels, independently of the colony process itself.

CPM-native chemotaxis (directed motion up a sensed gradient, e.g. the consumer moving toward the secretor's acetate plume rather than merely sitting in its path) remains out of scope for both regimes here, matching the flagship's own deferral.

The "viable-biomass floor" this study measures the competition loser against is the 1.25 seed biomass every cell starts at: a cell above its seed biomass is metabolically viable (net- growing or holding), one that has fallen below it is in net mass-loss toward death. This is a deliberately minimal, toy-real viability notion, not a fitted maintenance/decay bound; the process emits no explicit viability flag, so viability is read off the per-cell biomass observable. The point it establishes is honest and robust to the exact floor value: the competition loser ends at 64.5 (51.6x the floor), so it is displaced, not excluded.

The competition regime reaches NO true competitive exclusion over the run measured — it imposes no death and no viability constraint on a losing cell, so the loser (biomass 64.5, 81 px) is spatially displaced, not eliminated. The winner's 3511-px endpoint is ~97.5% of the 3600-px lattice with the field nearly spent by t=20, so that endpoint is partly a finite-size lattice-saturation artifact; extending the run to t≈30 fills the lattice and crowds the still- viable loser off it (eviction, not starvation). Strict exclusion would require coupling a viability constraint, not only shared state — the paper's §Cell–cell coupling distinction.

MULTI-SEED ROBUSTNESS (the headline is a range, not a single-seed point). The competition headline ratio (3.69x, id 1 / id 2 biomass) is a SINGLE-SEED reading of a stochastic CPM Metropolis trajectory. A 5-seed sweep (`tests/test_cellcell_multiseed.py`, seeds 1-5, CPM seed varied via the now config-overridable `CpmColonyField` seed) gives the honest range: ratio 2.9x-3.7x, mean ~3.2x -- the hard-coded single-seed 3.69x is the TOP of the band, not its middle. The qualitative claim is seed-robust: the faster competitor (id 1, glucose_vmax 10) wins on both biomass and lattice volume at every seed, always by > 1.5x. This study establishes the multi-seed convention for the investigation (process reads `seed` from config; deep-copy the composite state, sweep the seed, assert the qualitative claim per seed and report the numeric range); studies 5/7/9 copy the pattern rather than resting on a single hard-coded seed.

The secretor-knockout necessity control (`cellcell-crossfeed-knockout`) removes the secretor cell entirely rather than only silencing its acetate secretion in place; this is the cleanest single-variable knockout (no acetate source anywhere) and avoids a confound of the alternative (raising the secretor's O2 cap so it stops overflowing also makes it grow far faster and crowd the consumer off the lattice). The consumer is therefore the only cell in the control (id 1), and its glucose exchange stays off by role, so the slowly-diffusing glucose depot it cannot eat is harmless to the control.

It confirms a property HOLDS (mass is conserved to the expected value), so it is a positive/structural check.

findings.statement: Over the same coupling process, a different composite -- a localized glucose depot, a fast-diffusing acetate byproduct, and an acetate-consuming cell role -- sustains a cell that never touches glucose purely via a spatial metabolic handoff: the consumer's local glucose reads 0.0 the entire run while its biomass still climbs, entirely on diffused acetate. This is the paper's §Cell–cell coupling relational-molecule claim made concrete -- the same acetate is the secretor's metabolic waste and the consumer's sole carbon food, its meaning set by each cell's interface (microbial cross-feeding, morris2013). Confirmed: consumer local_glucose 0.0, local_acetate 1.30, biomass 1.25 -> 3.79, ending as a viable 65-pixel CPM cell.

The cross-feeding handoff is NECESSARY, not incidental: a secretor-knockout control (`cellcell-crossfeed-knockout` -- the cross-feed composite with the acetate secretor cell removed so no acetate is produced anywhere) leaves the otherwise-identical consumer unable to grow. It sits at local acetate 0.0 and its biomass never climbs off its 1.25 seed (persisting on the lattice at ~35 px), against the 1.25 -> 3.79 growth the same consumer shows when the secretor is present. This closes the handoff-necessity argument the flagship left resting only on local_glucose == 0.0 + observed growth: the consumer's growth is genuinely caused by the secretor's acetate, not by anything intrinsic to the consumer or the field.

findings.statement: The additive two-writer assumption `CpmColonyField`'s N-cell field update depends on -- that disjoint per-cell footprint deltas sum losslessly into one shared field -- is runtime-verified directly and independently of any dFBA mechanism, retiring what was previously an unverified assumption in the flagship study. Confirmed structurally: two synthetic single-pixel writers on disjoint pixels each apply independently and their combined effect exactly matches the sum of the two, over repeated ticks.

evidence.observed: two disjoint single-pixel writers each removing 1.0/tick over 3 ticks sum to a net field-wide change of exactly -6.0, with both individual pixels independently correct

regression_compatibility.basis: All three composites -- cellcell-compete.composite.json, cellcell-crossfeed.composite.json, and the new cellcell-crossfeed-knockout.composite.json -- build and run to completion through the process-bigraph engine (tests/test_cellcell_regimes.py, tests/test_cpm_colony_field.py, tests/test_cpm_colony_viz.py, tests/test_composites_build.py); guarded skip when the optional cobra/cpm/spatio_flux dependencies are absent, matching this investigation's flagship and draft-to-living-cell's own FBA-grain convention.

biological_validation.basis: All primary behavior tests pass on measured readouts from real 20-tick runs -- the competition regime drives a decisive biomass/volume split between two otherwise-identical competitors differing only in uptake capacity (asymmetric growth TOWARD competitive exclusion; the loser is displaced but stays viable, 51.6x above the viable-biomass floor, not driven below any viability bound -- this study couples shared state, not a viability constraint), and the cross-feeding regime sustains a consumer cell that never touches glucose purely via a diffused acetate handoff. Two structural/foundational verifications (the two-writer additivity check and the acetate-plume positive check) and a genuine negative control (the secretor-knockout -- with no acetate produced, the consumer flatly fails to grow, biomass held at its 1.25 seed) all pass, pinning both the mechanism and its necessity.

explanatory_gain.basis: Generalizing the flagship's single-cell CpmCellField to an N-cell CpmColonyField and demonstrating both branches of the paper's §Cell–cell coupling viability-negotiation pattern (no dedicated figure) -- shared-resource competition (asymmetric growth toward exclusion) AND cross-feeding -- from the same coupling process, differing only in the composite's cell roles and field constants, makes draft-to-living-cell's law-4 claim (different handlers over one interface negotiate a shared-resource constraint differently) concrete at real spatial, per-footprint dFBA resolution that its lumped two-role, shared- scalar-pool analogue could not reach. The secretor-knockout control further pins the cross-feeding handoff as necessary, not incidental.

conclusion:
## Claims
- Composing N real CPM cells with one shared, real spatio-flux nutrient field through a single N-cell coupling process (`CpmColonyField`) reproduces the paper's §Cell–cell coupling viability-negotiation pattern (no dedicated figure) as genuine spatial multicellularity. Over 20-tick runs: an uptake-capacity asymmetry alone (glucose_vmax 10 vs 4) drives asymmetric growth TOWARD competitive exclusion (biomass 237.9 vs 64.5, 3.69x; volume 3511 vs 81 px) -- the loser is spatially displaced but stays viable (its biomass grew ~51.6x above the 1.25 seed floor), not driven below a viability bound, and the winner's ~97.5%-lattice endpoint is partly a finite-size saturation artifact, so strict exclusion is not reached; a different composite over the same process -- localized glucose depot, fast-diffusing acetate byproduct, acetate-consuming role -- sustains a cell that never touches glucose (local glucose 0.0) purely via a diffusing cross-feeding handoff (local acetate 1.30, biomass 1.25 -> 3.79), and a secretor-knockout control shows that handoff is necessary (no acetate -> consumer held at its 1.25 seed).

## Evidence
- **COMPETITION-EXCLUDES-THE-SLOWER-CELL** -- biomass 237.9 (id 1) vs 64.5 (id 2), 3.69x margin
- **COMPETITION-VOLUME-TRACKS-BIOMASS** -- CPM volume 3511 px (id 1) vs 81 px (id 2)
- **COMPETITION-LOSER-DISPLACED-NOT-EXCLUDED** -- loser biomass 64.5 (51.6x the 1.25 viable- biomass floor): displaced (81 px vs winner 3511 px ~97.5% of the lattice), not excluded
- **CROSSFEEDING-CONSUMER-BLIND-TO-GLUCOSE** -- consumer local_glucose == 0.0
- **CROSSFEEDING-CONSUMER-GROWS-ON-ACETATE-ALONE** -- consumer biomass 1.25 -> 3.79 on acetate alone
- **CROSSFEEDING-ACETATE-PLUME-REACHES-CONSUMER** (positive check) -- consumer local_acetate == 1.30 by t=20
- **CROSSFEEDING-SECRETOR-KNOCKOUT-CONSUMER-FAILS-TO-GROW** (negative control) -- secretor removed, no acetate produced, consumer biomass held at its 1.25 seed (vs 1.25 -> 3.79)
- **TWO-WRITER-ADDITIVITY-CONSERVES-MASS** (structural check) -- disjoint per-cell field writes sum losslessly, runtime-verified

## Limitations
- "Competitive exclusion" is not literally reached over the run: the loser is displaced (81 px, biomass 64.5) but stays viable -- this study couples shared state, not a viability constraint, so no cell is driven below a viability bound (§Cell–cell coupling: what is coupled is not only state, but constraint -- here, only state). The winner's 3511-px (~97.5% of 3600) endpoint is partly a finite-size lattice-saturation artifact; at t≈30 the winner fills the lattice and the still-viable loser is crowded off it (eviction, not starvation).
- e_coli_core-derived constants (glucose_vmax, acetate_vmax, grow_per_biomass, the O2 cap) are toy-real -- plausible, hand-tuned magnitudes, not fitted to any organism or medium.
- The cross-feeding regime's acetate/glucose diffusion ratio (15.0 vs 0.4) is directionally defensible (acetate is a smaller molecule) but was chosen, not fitted; the localized glucose depot is a deliberately engineered spatial arrangement, not a naturally arising gradient.
- The consumer's growth under cross-feeding is back-loaded to roughly the last 5 ticks of the run, once the acetate plume has had time to diffuse across the distance between the two cells' footprints -- monotonic over the measured window, not smoothly exponential from tick 0.
- Each CPM cell gets its own independent cobra model copy, not one shared model instance across the colony.
- CPM-native chemotaxis (directed motion toward a sensed gradient) remains out of scope for both regimes here.
## Next steps
- Extend `CpmColonyField` to N > 2 cells to test whether the competitive/cross-feeding pattern generalizes to population-scale spatial negotiation.
- Add CPM-native chemotaxis so the consumer can move toward the sensed acetate plume rather than merely sitting in its path.
- Fan out to the next spatial counterpart in the design spec's increment plan.

if_primary_tests_pass.implementation_status: Both cellcell-compete.composite.json and cellcell-crossfeed.composite.json build and run to completion through the engine over 20 ticks.
if_primary_tests_pass.biological_validation: The spatial §Cell–cell coupling viability-negotiation pattern (no dedicated figure) is demonstrated at the toy-real (uncalibrated) level, with genuine per-cell CPM shape dynamics and independent dFBA solves behind both the shared-resource-competition (asymmetric growth toward exclusion; loser displaced, not excluded) and cross-feeding branches, rather than a scripted trajectory. The cross-feeding handoff is pinned as necessary by the secretor-knockout control (no acetate -> no consumer growth).

diagnose: the faster competitor's biomass/volume margin over the slower one collapses (uptake-capacity asymmetry not taking effect, or the shared field is not actually being depleted by both cells)
the consumer's local glucose is not near-zero (the localized glucose depot is leaking into the consumer's footprint, defeating the cross-feeding demonstration)
the consumer's biomass never rises despite zero local glucose (the acetate plume is not reaching it, or the consumer's acetate uptake/growth coupling is broken)
the secretor-knockout consumer DOES grow despite no acetate being produced (the observed cross-feeding growth was not actually caused by the secretor's acetate -- necessity broken)
the two-writer additivity control fails to conserve mass (the N-cell field-write assumption CpmColonyField depends on is broken)
if_primary_tests_fail.block_downstream: future N>2-cell population-scale spatial studies, all of which reuse CpmColonyField or its coupling pattern

limitations: "Competitive exclusion" is not literally reached: the competition loser is spatially displaced (ends at 81 px, biomass 64.5 -- still 51.6x above its 1.25 seed / viable-biomass floor) but is never driven below a viability bound. This study couples shared STATE (one field) but no viability CONSTRAINT (no death, no viability bound on a losing cell), so the honest phenomenon is asymmetric growth TOWARD exclusion, not exclusion. The winner's 3511-px endpoint is ~97.5% of the 3600-px lattice with the field nearly exhausted by t=20, so that endpoint is partly a finite-size lattice-saturation artifact; extending the run to t≈30 fills the lattice and crowds the still-viable loser off it (eviction, not starvation), which a viability-constraint coupling would be needed to turn into genuine exclusion.

The competition headline ratio (3.69x biomass, id 1 / id 2) is a single-seed number; a 5-seed robustness sweep (tests/test_cellcell_multiseed.py) puts the honest range at ~2.9x-3.7x (mean ~3.2x), with the single-seed 3.69x at the top of the band and the faster competitor winning every seed by > 1.5x. See key_assumptions for the convention this establishes for the investigation.

e_coli_core-derived constants (glucose_vmax, acetate_vmax, grow_per_biomass, the O2 cap) are toy-real, hand-tuned magnitudes chosen to make both regimes legible over a short run -- not fitted to any organism or medium.

The cross-feeding regime's acetate/glucose diffusion ratio (15.0 vs 0.4) is directionally defensible -- acetate is a smaller molecule and diffuses faster than glucose in real aqueous media -- but the specific ratio was chosen to make the plume legibly reach the consumer within 20 ticks, not fitted to measured diffusion coefficients; the localized 20 mM glucose depot is likewise a deliberately engineered spatial arrangement so the consumer genuinely sees zero glucose, not a naturally arising gradient.

The consumer's growth under cross-feeding is back-loaded to roughly the last 5 ticks of the 20-tick run, once the secretor's acetate plume has had time to diffuse across the distance separating the two cells' footprints -- monotonic over the measured window, but not smoothly exponential from tick 0.
Each CPM cell in CpmColonyField gets its own independent cobra model copy, not one shared model instance across the colony.

The additive two-writer assumption CpmColonyField's N-cell field-write depends on is now runtime-verified directly (tests/test_cpm_colony_two_writer.py), independent of both regimes' own dFBA mechanism -- previously an unverified assumption inherited from the flagship study.

The secretor-knockout necessity control removes the secretor CELL entirely (cleanest single- variable knockout: no acetate source anywhere) rather than silencing acetate secretion in place; the alternative -- raising the secretor's O2 cap so it stops overflowing -- also makes it grow far faster and crowd the consumer off the lattice, a confound the cell-removal avoids. The control therefore establishes that acetate is necessary for the consumer's growth, but not the finer counterfactual of an in-place, same-growth secretor that merely stops secreting.
CPM-native chemotaxis (directed motion up a sensed gradient) remains out of scope for both regimes here, matching the flagship's own deferral.
falsifiability: Overturned if the faster competitor's biomass/volume margin over the slower competitor collapses under the competition regime, if the shared glucose field is not measurably depleted (the cells not genuinely coupled through one field), if the cross-feeding consumer's local glucose is not near-zero (the localized depot leaking into its footprint), if the consumer's biomass fails to rise despite zero local glucose (the acetate handoff not actually sustaining it), if the secretor-knockout consumer nonetheless grows despite no acetate being produced (the cross-feeding growth not actually caused by the secretor's acetate -- necessity broken), or if the additive two-writer field control fails to conserve mass (the N-cell field-write assumption CpmColonyField depends on broken).

experiment: Run two `CpmColonyField` composites -- `cellcell-compete` (two glucose competitors, glucose_vmax 10.0 vs 4.0, one shared uniform glucose field) and `cellcell-crossfeed` (a glucose-to-acetate secretor plus an acetate-consuming cell, a localized glucose depot, and a fast-diffusing acetate byproduct) -- each to completion over 20 ticks through the process- bigraph engine, and measure whether uptake-capacity asymmetry alone drives spatial competitive exclusion, and whether a diffusing metabolic byproduct alone can sustain a cell that never touches its nominal nutrient.
result: Over 20-tick runs, the competition regime drives a decisive spatial split from uptake- capacity asymmetry alone (biomass 237.9 vs 64.5, 3.69x; CPM volume 3511 vs 81 px) -- asymmetric growth TOWARD competitive exclusion, though not exclusion reached: the loser is displaced but still viable (its biomass grew ~51.6x, far above the 1.25 seed floor), never driven below a viability bound, and the winner's ~97.5%-lattice endpoint is partly a finite-size saturation artifact -- this study couples shared state, not a viability constraint. The cross-feeding regime -- the same `CpmColonyField` process, a different composite -- sustains a consumer cell that never touches glucose (local glucose 0.0) purely via a diffusing acetate handoff (local acetate 1.30, biomass 1.25 -> 3.79, ending as a viable 65-pixel CPM cell), and a secretor-knockout control confirms that handoff is necessary (secretor removed, no acetate produced, the consumer held at its 1.25 seed). The paper's §Cell–cell coupling viability-negotiation pattern (no dedicated figure) holds as genuine spatial multicellularity, composed from independent frameworks through one N-cell coupling process, one interface, two regimes. The cross-feeding regime also carries the paper's closing relational-molecule claim (§Cell–cell coupling): the same acetate is metabolic waste to the secretor and sole carbon food to the consumer -- and, in `disintegration-spatial`, a toxin whose accumulation crosses a cell's viability bound -- one molecule whose meaning is set relationally by each cell's interface.

biological_validation.basis: All primary behavior tests pass on measured readouts from real 20-tick runs -- the competition regime drives a decisive biomass/volume split between two otherwise-identical competitors differing only in uptake capacity (asymmetric growth TOWARD competitive exclusion; the loser is displaced but stays viable, 51.6x above the viable-biomass floor, not driven below any viability bound -- this study couples shared state, not a viability constraint), and the cross-feeding regime sustains a consumer cell that never touches glucose purely via a diffused acetate handoff. Two structural/foundational verifications (the two-writer additivity check and the acetate-plume positive check) and a genuine negative control (the secretor-knockout -- with no acetate produced, the consumer flatly fails to grow, biomass held at its 1.25 seed) all pass, pinning both the mechanism and its necessity.

regression_compatibility.basis: All three composites -- cellcell-compete.composite.json, cellcell-crossfeed.composite.json, and the new cellcell-crossfeed-knockout.composite.json -- build and run to completion through the process-bigraph engine (tests/test_cellcell_regimes.py, tests/test_cpm_colony_field.py, tests/test_cpm_colony_viz.py, tests/test_composites_build.py); guarded skip when the optional cobra/cpm/spatio_flux dependencies are absent, matching this investigation's flagship and draft-to-living-cell's own FBA-grain convention.

explanatory_gain.basis: Generalizing the flagship's single-cell CpmCellField to an N-cell CpmColonyField and demonstrating both branches of the paper's §Cell–cell coupling viability-negotiation pattern (no dedicated figure) -- shared-resource competition (asymmetric growth toward exclusion) AND cross-feeding -- from the same coupling process, differing only in the composite's cell roles and field constants, makes draft-to-living-cell's law-4 claim (different handlers over one interface negotiate a shared-resource constraint differently) concrete at real spatial, per-footprint dFBA resolution that its lumped two-role, shared- scalar-pool analogue could not reach. The secretor-knockout control further pins the cross-feeding handoff as necessary, not incidental.

derived.insight: Multiple real CPM cells sharing one real spatio-flux nutrient field through one N-cell coupling process (`CpmColonyField`) reproduce the paper's §Cell–cell coupling shared-resource-competition branch (no dedicated figure) as genuine spatial multicellularity: an uptake-capacity asymmetry alone (glucose_vmax 10 vs 4), with each cell running its own independent dFBA solve at its own footprint on the same depleting field, drives a decisive biomass and lattice-volume split -- asymmetric growth TOWARD competitive exclusion. Confirmed: biomass 237.9 vs 64.5 (3.69x), CPM volume 3511 vs 81 px, over a 20-tick run. (Strict exclusion is not reached -- the loser is displaced but stays viable; see F-04.)
